newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan offers China loan, cooperation on markets.
newsitem.headline: Japan offers China loan, cooperation on markets.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Wednesday promised China more economic assistance and called for cooperation between Tokyo and Beijing to help stabilise financial markets, a Japanese official said.

Mitsuzuka held talks with Chinese Premier Li Peng who said the strengthening of the yen would add to China's loan repayment burden because of Beijing's high level of yen-denominated loans, a Japanese finance official quoted Li as saying.
The two agreed in their talks that currency stability was important, the official said.
Mitsuzuka passed on a message to Li from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, saying he was looking forward to Li's visit in early September. Hashimoto is expected to visit China in November.

The Export-Import Bank of Japan would extend $700 million in untied loans to China, and Tokyo would this year hold a meeting for Asian emerging nations and international organisations on stability, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said.
"We would like to cooperate with China for financial market stability," the official quoted Mitsuzuka, who began a four-day visit to China on Tuesday, as saying.

Japan and China had agreed to hold working level meetings later in the year on China's participation in the international meeting, which would group emerging Asian nations with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, the official told a news briefing.
Officials from China's Ministry of Finance and the People's Bank of China, the central bank, would take part.
"My impression was that the Chinese side was positive about the idea," the official said.
Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the MOF's International Finance Bureau, had attended the ministerial meeting and said Tokyo had already taken initiatives to promote market stability.

Tokyo had held a first meeting of six Pacific economies in March, when Japan, China, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore had agreed to strengthen cooperation and information exchanges to boost stability, he said.
The Tokyo meeting was scheduled to be followed by another gathering of the six in Singapore next year, he said.

Mitsuzuku, whose visit to China is partly aimed at repairing Sino-Japanese ties battered by territorial and strategic differences, also brought more concrete assistance for Japan's huge Asian neighbour.

Mitsuzuka told Chinese Finance Minister Liu Zhongli that the Export-Import Bank of Japan would approve a request from China for $700 million worth of untied loans to finance 10 infrastructure and industrial projects, officials said.
The projects included a trunk road project in China's southeastern city of Xiamen and and the construction of a steel processing factory in the central city of Wuhan.

Mitsuzuka, who came straight to China after a summit of the Group of Seven industrialised nations in Denver at the weekend, told Liu that Japan told the G7 nations it supported China's bid for long-delayed accession to the World Trade Organisation.
